dedupe_keys.name: asset level assessment of climate physical risk for adaptation finance in mexico nature communications 2024

description: This case study presents a method that quantifies climate physical risk on geolocated productive assets, from both chronic climate impacts and acute hurricanes across the scenarios of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and then translates the asset-level shocks into economic losses for firms and financial losses for their investors. It was carried out by Giacomo Bressan, Anja Đuranović, Irene Monasterolo and Stefano Battiston and published in Nature Communications on 1 July 2024. The method is applied to Mexico, a country highly exposed to physical risks and a recipient of adaptation finance and foreign investment; coverage is national. The article is open access under CC BY 4.0. The authors find that investor losses are underestimated by up to 70% when asset-level information is neglected and by up to 82% when tail acute risks are neglected, so aggregate approaches misjudge adaptation needs. Caveats: the metadata read give the abstract only, so the hazard models, asset databases and data availability must be checked in the article itself. For simulation it shows how to link hazard exposure of individual industrial and energy assets to financial losses, a pattern for climate adaptation and investment appraisal studies of infrastructure. It is related to the Orbis company database record in this catalogue, a common source of firm ownership links for such analyses.
